title: Jensen Huang at Startup School: how a wrong bet, textbooks and "how hard can it be?" built NVIDIA
summary: Jensen tells how NVIDIA's founding technology was wrong, how a Sega contract and three textbooks saved it, and why accelerating algorithm domains beat building chips. He covers first-principles curiosity, fitting the company to the founder, systems thinking, agents, physical AI, and resilience: get through today.

principles.text: Confront reality and learn: technology changes, so willingness to learn matters more than your starting technology.
principles.quote: technology is changing all the time and so long as you're able to confront the reality so long as you are able to learn the technology itself actually doesn't matter.

principles.text: Great companies come from a unique, deeply held perspective on the future, not just the chip or the market.
principles.quote: what makes great companies is a unique perspective about the world that you deeply believe in. It's not so much the technology, it's not so much uh the market even

principles.text: Accelerate an algorithm domain, not just build a chip.
principles.quote: it's not about building a great chip, it's about accelerating an algorithm domain.

principles.text: Fit the company to the founder, like an F1 car built so you can drive it; keep tweaking it.
principles.quote: You're going to build an F1 racer, but you're going to build it in a way that you can drive. You should adapt the car to you.

principles.text: Reason from first principles about what you observe: if this, then what? Live 5 to 10 years in the future.
principles.quote: asking questions, reasoning about things to first principles, asking you know questions like if this then what?

principles.text: Resilience: take on the problem with 'how hard can it be?' and just get through today.
principles.quote: You don't have to overcome life in one day you just have to overcome that morning
